Mansur Habib with Lutfunnessa Lucky, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners.

Abdul Kader Rabbani and others ------ Petitioners 
vs 
Ebaruddin and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-13 to show cause as to why the impugned order complained of in the petition should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The case of the petitioners, in short, is that the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners and opposite party Nos. 14-28 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 96 of 1956 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge) Rangpur, for declaration of title' of 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule land and for khas possession of the 'ka' schedule land against the predecessor-in-interest of the opposite party Nos. 1-13 and other defendants. The suit was decreed on contest with costs against the contesting defendants and ex parte against the rest and the title of the plaintiffs to the disputed land was declared and it was also declared that the plaintiffs would get khas possession in the 'Ka' schedule land by evicting the defendants therefrom by the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1961. Being aggrieved the contesting defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 141 of 1961 in the Court of District Judge, Rangpur and the said appeal was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 24-7-1962. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below, the appellant preferred second Appeal No. 625 of 1966 in the High Court of Judicature at Dacca in the then East Pakistan and the second Appeal No. 625 of 1966 was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 1-2-1980. During pendency of the second Appeal No. 625 of 1966 there was no order of stay of the execution proceeding and the decree holder put the decree into execution being Title Execution No. 36 of 1969 and during the proceeding of the said execution case the judgment-debtor filed.an application under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, putting objection that one of the decree holders Abdul Aziz was an Indian National and, 'as such, the decree was not executable and the application under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1975. The Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1975 was allowed and the executing Court held that the decree cannot be executed as one of the decree holders was an Indian National and further ordered that the Title Execution Case No. 36 of 1969 be struck off by the order dated 8-7-1975. Being aggrieved the decree holder  preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 25 of 1976 in the Court of District Judge, Rangpur and the said appeal was disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Rangpur who upheld the order of the Executing Court by judgment and order dated 31-8- 1977. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order the decree holders preferred second Miscellaneous Appeal No. 22 of 1978 and the said appeal was disposed of at the Rangpur Session of the High Court Division and the High Court Division allowed the appeal holding that there was no materials on record to show that Abdul Aziz was an Indian National and sent the appeal on remand to take fresh evidence whether Abdul Aziz was an Indian National or not by the judgment and order dated 16- 3-1988. In the meantime, Lalmonirhat Judgeship started functioning and Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1975 along with Title Execution Case No. 36 of 1969 was transferred to that Judgeship and Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1975 was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1992. The Subordinate Judge, Lalmonirhat after taking oral and documentary evidence held that one of the decree holders was an Indian National and, as such, 112 share of the suit land was not executable and, as such, 1/2 share of the suit land the other decree holder was entitled to take delivery of possession after executing the Title Execution Case No. 36 of 1969 by the judgment and order dated 30-3-1992. Being aggrieved, the heirs of decree holder Abdul Aziz preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.8 of 1992 in the Court of District Judge, Lalmonirhat. The learned District Judge, Lalmonirhat on 16-7-1992 took up the Miscellaneous Appeal No.8 of 1992 for admission hearing and after hearing the appellants held that since section 47 CPC has been omitted by the Ordinance XLVIII of 1983 the Subordinate Judge had no jurisdiction to entertain any matter under section 47 of the CPC and, as such, the Miscellaneous Appeal was not maintainable and dismissed the same overlooking the direction of the High Court Division in second Miscellaneous Appeal No. 22 of 1978.

3. It is stated that during promulgation of Ordinance No. XLVIII of 1983 the second Miscellaneous Appeal No. 22 of 1978 arising out of the application under section 47 CPC was pending and in disposal of the said second Miscellaneous Appeal the High Court Division sent the appeal on remand to dispose of the matter after taking fresh evidence to the effect whether one of the decree holders Abdul Aziz was an Indian National or not. In continuation of the said order the Subordinate Judge disposed of the matter and the learned District Judge erred in law in not admitting the Miscellaneous Appeal No.8 of 1992.

4. Being aggrieved, the petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

5. We have heard Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, as none appeared for the opposite parties.

6. It is not disputed that Abdul Aziz predecessor-in-interest of 13 decree holder petitioners and Nazaruddin Ahmed, predecessor-in-interest of opposite party Nos. 14-28 instituted Title Suit No. 96 of 1959 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Rangpur for declaration of title in respect of 5.16 acres of land as mentioned in 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule land and for recovery of possession in the 'Ka' schedule land measuring 4.93 acres of land. The suit was decreed on contest and the appeal being Title Appeal No. 141 of 1969 against the decree was dismissed and also second Appeal No. 625 of 1966 was also dismissed by the High Court Division on 1-2-1980. During pendency of the second Appeal before the High Court the plaintiffs- decree holders filed Title Execution Case No. 36 of 1969 and put the decree into execution as there was no stay order from the High Court Division. The judgment-debtor filed objection Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1975 under section 47 of the CPC on the ground that one of the decree holders, Abdul Aziz, was an Indian National. The objection Miscellaneous Case was allowed on contest and the Execution Case was struck off. Miscellaneous Appeal No. 25 of 1976 filed by the decree holder against the said order was also dismissed. Against the appellate order the decree holder filed second Miscellaneous Appeal No. 22 of 1978 before the High Court Division. During pendency of the above mentioned Second Miscellaneous Appeal, the Second Appeal was dismissed on 1- 2-1980. Thereafter, on 2-10-1981 the decree holders filed another Execution case being Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1982 for execution of the decree and got delivery of possession in the 'Ka' schedule land through Court on 31- 7 -1982. Second Miscellaneous Appeal as mentioned above was allowed by the High Court Division on 16-3-1988 and the matter was sent back on remand to the Executing Court for further investigation as to the status of Abdul Aziz in the objection case. In the meantime, a separate Judgeship was created at Lalmonirhat and objection Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1975 transferred there and remembered as Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 1990. The learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) by judgment and order dated 30-3-1992 held that the decree in respect of 8 annas share of the plaintiff Abdul Aziz was not executable. Against this order the heirs of Abdul Aziz preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.8 of 1992 before the District Judge who summarily dismissed the same on 16-7-1992 and against the said order the decree holder obtained Rule in the instant case on 21-10-1992.

<u>7. Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Advocated for the petitioner, mainly argued that objection Miscellaneous Case under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed in 1975 and the same was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1975 and when the case was transferred to the learned Subordinate Judge, Lalmonirhat after creation of new Judgeship the same was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 1990. The learned Subordinate Judge, Lalmonirhat (now Joint District Judge) by his judgment and order dated 30-3-1992 held that the decree in respect of 8 annas share of the plaintiff Abdul Aziz was not executable. Against this order the heirs of Abdul Aziz preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 1992 before the District Judge, Lalmonirhat who summarily dismissed the appeal on 16-7-1992 and against the said order the decree holder petitioners obtained the present Rule on 21-10-1992. He submits that since the application under section 47 of the CPC was filed in 1975 and numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1975, the same was pending when Ordinance No. XLVIII of 1983 came into force and by section 3 of the Ordinance section 47, CPC was deleted/omitted. But since the application under section 47, CPC was pending the same will be saved by the provision of section 6 of the General Clauses Act as pending proceeding. He further submits that notwithstanding the repeal of section 47, CPC as per provision of section 6 of General Clauses Act the same would not affect any legal proceeding and, as such, the proceeding shall continue as if there has been no repeal of section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure. A civil proceeding includes execution proceeding as well as appeal also.</u>

8. In the above facts and circumstances and in view of my above discussion, I am of the view that the learned District Judge was not justified in rejecting the memo of appeal on the assumption that since section 47, CPC was repealed no appeal against the proceeding under the repealed law can continue. In my opinion this is a fit case where this Court should interfere and send the case back on remand to the learned District Judge to dispose of the matter in accordance with law.

9. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The order dated 16-7-1992 passed by the learned District Judge, Lalmonirhat in Miscellaneous Appeal No.8 of 1992 is hereby set aside and the case is sent back on remand to the said Court to dispose of the matter in accordance with law and in the light of the observation made in the body of the judgment.

Send down the LC record at once.

End.
